releaseNotes.summary: Juno Beta 0.3 Hotfix 1 repairs ChatGPT plan sign-in packaging and adds a guarded factory reset that returns Juno to its genuine first-run setup.
highlights: The Windows DPAPI credential helper is built, staged and verified by the packaged app before ChatGPT credentials are stored.
A pinned Codex runtime is bundled for ChatGPT plan sign-in, while independently installed Codex remains untouched.
Settings → General → Reset Juno erases Juno-owned bots, conversations, memory, routines, teams, results, provider credentials and preferences, then reopens onboarding.
External projects, the Juno installation, protocol registration, update trust and other applications' credentials are preserved.
improvements: ChatGPT setup distinguishes a missing Codex runtime, unavailable credential protection, a cancelled browser sign-in, an ineligible plan and a usage limit.
Codex discovery also finds user-local npm, pnpm, winget, scoop and sandbox installs, and rechecks after a runtime is installed.
A reset interrupted by a crash or reboot is completed on the next launch before any server or window starts.
fixes: Fixed the packaged app reporting `codex CLI not found` on a fresh Windows installation.
Fixed credential protection being unavailable because the DPAPI helper was never staged outside ASAR.
Fixed a missing prerequisite being shown as a failed ChatGPT account sign-in.
knownIssues: The Windows installer remains unsigned; automatic installation of unsigned updates is intentionally disabled.
A live ChatGPT sign-in still needs a real eligible account and owner authorization.
The NSIS installer itself is not executed on this development host to protect the owner's existing Beta installation.
releaseNotes.compatibility: Windows x64. Existing Beta profiles upgrade in place and keep their data unless the owner explicitly chooses Reset Juno.
